primitives.assumptions: Logarithmic utility, agent independence, complete markets, no arbitrage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When wealths become degenerate or beliefs collapse.

primitives.name: Product of Experts Equilibrium
primitives.verbatim_quote: u(w) = -exp(-a·w) (CARA) ⇒ demand ∝ log p_i ⇒ equilibrium price ∝ Π_i p_i^{weight_i} — product of experts; wealth drops out (irrelevant under CARA).

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that agent utility functions induce specific probabilistic model combinations at market equilibrium. Under logarithmic utility, agents optimize expected log wealth, leading to a weighted average of beliefs—this is the mixture of experts formulation. With exponential (CARA) utility, agents optimize expected exponential utility, which leads to a product of beliefs, i.e., product of experts. These mappings are mathematically rigorous and emerge from first-order optimality conditions under budget constraints. The equilibrium price vector becomes the predictive distribution of a combined model whose form depends on the utility functions. This duality allows GSE to treat model ensembling as an optimization problem over agent utilities rather than ad hoc weighting schemes. The key failure mode arises when beliefs are degenerate or utilities are non-concave, breaking equilibrium existence. Additionally, the assumption of complete markets may not hold in practice, limiting direct application to sparse or high-dimensional outcome spaces.
